proposals.relationship: Gordon credits Alice Clark’s1919study with shaping her understanding of gender as a material practice.

proposals.relationship: Gordon disputes Scott’s account of agency, defending action through unequal parties’ conflicts and a distinction between violence and its representations (1990).
proposals.evidence_note: Selected primary continuationp853: Gordon retains social-control analysis while rejecting the interpretation of her argument she attributes to Scott. Page852 and the subsequent book-review exchange remain unread. This specific reply does not establish a blanket rejection of Scott or discourse analysis.

proposals.relationship: Scott questions Gordon’s conception of agency in Heroes of Their Own Lives, proposing a discursive account rather than an autonomous individual attribute (1990).
proposals.evidence_note: As reconstructed by Megan Clare Webber, introductionp7 and notes20–23, citing Scott’s reviewp851. The Scott original remains unread. A specific interpretive objection, not a claim that Scott denies historical action. Gordon’s separate reply is directly witnessed on853.

proposals.relationship: Uses child-protection case records to reconstruct family power and negotiated social intervention, challenging the assumption of a formerly autonomous family (1983–84).
proposals.evidence_note: Selected own article529–534: poor women and children can initiate outside intervention despite unequal power and real violence. This contributes to the family-history strand of the combined demography/family entry; it does not establish a demographic method or field foundation. Distinct from the existing women’s-history and Arizona racial-formation claims.
